title: Could Paying Attention to Pain Help You Heal?
paragraphs: When something in your body hurts, you may try to distract yourself from the pain. You might watch a video, talk to a friend or just think about something that makes you happy.
But what happens when you do the opposite, and pay more attention to the pain?
Researchers at Bar-Ilan University in Israel used several experiments to see if paying attention to pain can change how the body reacts to it.

In the first experiment, 37 people received a histamine skin prick on their arm. Histamine is a chemical in your body that reacts to things you're allergic to, and the test caused a small reaction on the skin, including swelling and redness.
For the next 20 minutes, participants either focused on the itching and burning feelings, or watched videos to distract themselves.
Around 90% of participants had more swelling and redness when they were distracted. On average, the swelling and redness were about 1.5 times greater for distracted participants.
But when people focused on the pain in their arm, the reaction was smaller and started returning to normal more quickly.
The team did another experiment with 20 people. This time, everyone looked at shapes on a screen. Some were told to focus on the feelings in their arm, while others were told to focus on the shapes.
Again, 90% had a larger inflammatory reaction when they focused on the shapes.
So why might paying attention to pain help it end faster?

Paying attention may influence the way the brain processes the signals from the affected area, which could affect how the body reacts to it. When people paid attention to the pain, the researchers also found signs of increased activity in the vagal nerves, which are long nerves that run from the brain to the intestines and help control inflammation.
The researchers say this suggests that we may be able to affect our body's inflammatory reactions just by paying attention!
